examples.text: Нове́йшими иссле́дованиями устано́влено, что в лу́ке соде́ржатся не то́лько са́хар, белки́, минера́льные со́ли, но и осо́бые вещества́ — фитонци́ды, убива́ющие болезнетво́рные бакте́рии.

glosses: книжн. являющийся причиною или возбудителем болезни

examples.text: Они подобны болезнетворным микробам в желудке города, и будет время, когда они его отравят теми же ядами, которыми он так щедро питает их теперь!
malignant temper; malignant revenge; malignant infection
[…]while, I fear, there will be some white ones, unable to forget that, with malignant heart, and deceitful speech, they have strove to hinder it.

glosses: Tending to produce death; threatening a fatal issue.

examples.text: “[…] the awfully hearty sort of Christmas cards that people do send to other people that they don't know at all well. You know. The kind that have mottoes[…]. And then, when you see [the senders], you probably find that they are the most melancholy old folk with malignant diseases. […]”

glosses: A deviant; a person who is hostile or destructive to society.

examples.text: A malignant in a position of real power immediately becomes a tyrant.
As devout Stephen was carried to his burial by devout men, so is it just and equal that malignants should carry malignants […]

glosses: A person who fought for Charles I in the English Civil War.

examples.text: He accepted that the body was a machine, mathematically understandable, but disease was the effort by nature or the soul to expel morbific matter, and physiology was the science of that struggle.

glosses: Pertaining to or caused by disease; diseased.
